name: Lomé
subtitle: Lomé, capital of Togo: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 2,188,376 people live in Greater Lomé (counted 2022).
In the 2022 census the Golfe prefecture counted 1,305,681 people.
German governor August Köhler made Lomé the capital of Togo, and a palace was built for him between 1898 and 1905.

parts.text: In the 2022 census the Golfe prefecture counted 1,305,681 people.
German governor August Köhler made Lomé the capital of Togo, and a palace was built for him between 1898 and 1905.
The governor's palace was built to be recognisable from a long distance so that it would impress ships at sea.
Lomé's first wharf was a wooden one built by the Germans in 1890; after a fire it was replaced in 1904 by a second wharf of steel frames on concrete piles.
Togo became independent on 27 April 1960, and on 20 July of that year a German-Togolese agreement was signed to build a port.
The deep-water Port of Lomé received its first ship alongside, the Birte Hugo Stinnes, on 21 January 1967.
Annual port traffic grew from 252,600 tonnes in 1968 to 402,600 tonnes in 1972.
In 2024 the Port of Lomé handled 2.06 million containers (TEU), up 8% on the year before.
The Port of Lomé ranks 92nd in Lloyd's List's 2025 top 100 container ports and is the only sub-Saharan African port in that list.
The Port of Lomé is described as the only deep-water port of the sub-region.
The Palais de Lomé, a restored colonial palace, is described as the only contemporary art centre in Africa fully financed by the state.
The Akodessewa fetish market in Lomé covers more than 1,000 m2.

blocks.prompt: About how many people do you think live in Greater Lomé?

parts.text: 2,188,376 in 2022, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Grand Lomé region (Golfe plus Agoè-Nyivé prefectures); the Golfe prefecture alone counted 1,305,681.

items.text: The Germans built a wooden wharf on metal piles at Lomé.
Construction of the governor's palace began, ordered by Governor August Köhler.
A second wharf, of steel frames on concrete piles, replaced the first after a fire.
The French opened their own wharf at Lomé.
Togolese authorities decided to build a deep-water port because the French wharf could not cope.
The first stone of the deep-water port of Lomé was laid on 23 November.
The first ship, the Birte Hugo Stinnes, came alongside at the new port on 21 January.
The Grand Marché de Lomé burned in the night of 11 to 12 January.
The Palais de Lomé opened to the public as an art centre on 28 November.
The fifth census counted 2,188,376 people in Grand Lomé.
The Port of Lomé rose to 92nd in Lloyd's List's top 100 container ports.
